result.title: Neural Dimensional Analysis: Foundations of Dimensionless and Scale-Consistent Computation
result.summary: Modern Transformers rely on many scale-control mechanisms, including normalization, residual scaling, attention temperatures, loss weighting, and adaptive updates. To explain how these mechanisms maintain scale consistency, we introduce Neural Dimensional Analysis (NDA), a unified framework based on dimensional consistency. We define neural units that specify how tensors rescale and which quantities can be added, just as physical units do in physics. Our rules match residual units, nondimensionalize attention and gate inputs, combine losses across units, and convert gradient units into parameter units. We implement NDA through dimensionless Unit Violation Indices (UVI) for diagnosing scale mismatches within Transformers, a unit-consistent multi-loss objective, and the Gauge-Canonical Transformer (GCT) with normalized coordinates and orthogonalized residual additions. In language-model experiments spanning 51M to 1B parameters, GCT remains stable during training across a broad sixteenfold learning-rate range, outperforming Pre-LN, LLaMA-style, and QK-Norm in 124M validation loss at tuned learning rates. GCT's normalized residual stream also shows improved robustness to quantization. At 1B parameters, calibrated per-tensor int8 quantization increases GCT's validation loss by only 0.009 nats, compared with up to 5.51 nats for the baselines. Vision and physics-informed neural network experiments further confirm NDA's benefits beyond language modeling. These results establish dimensional consistency as a neural network design principle.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Neural Dimensional Analysis 框架，用类似物理量纲的「神经单位」刻画张量如何缩放、哪些量可相加，并据此给出诊断尺度失配的 Unit Violation Index、单位一致的多损失目标，以及采用归一化坐标与正交化残差相加的 Gauge-Canonical Transformer；在 51M–1B 语言模型上验证训练稳定性与量化鲁棒性。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作本身不涉及多模态推理，但其关于残差流尺度一致性、归一化坐标与量纲式诊断的线索，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态范数漂移、latent 相似度比较是否被尺度主导，以及循环/多步状态更新如何保持尺度一致。
